· did not start · working-directory
                                                                          
 ▎✗ ran go test ./...                        did not start · working dir  
                                                                          
     ▎✗ go test ./...                        did not start · working dir  
        working directory unavailable: /work/.claude/worktrees/gone —     
        chdir /bin/bash: no such file or directory                        
        Nothing ran: a command's working directory has to be there when   
        it starts. Find out where it went — a worktree or checkout        
        removed under a running session is the usual cause — and run the  
        command somewhere that still exists.                              
                                                                          


· did not start · execution-shell

     ▎✗ go test ./...                    did not start · execution shell  
        execution shell unavailable: fork/exec /usr/local/bin/bash: no    
        such file or directory                                            
        Nothing ran, and nothing will until that shell is back: every     
        command here goes through it, so another spelling of the same     
        command reaches the same missing program. Report it.

        containment unavailable: fork/exec /usr/bin/bwrap: no such file

        Nothing ran, and it was not run uncontained — that is the one     
        substitution this session will not make. Report the mechanism as

· did not start · permission
                                                                          
 ▎✗ ran ./deploy.sh                           did not start · permission  
                                                                          
     ▎✗ ./deploy.sh                           did not start · permission  
        permission denied: fork/exec ./deploy.sh: permission denied       
        Nothing ran. The refusal is the operating system's and not a      
        decision this session made or can undo, so use a program and a    
        path the current user is already allowed, or report what is       
        refusing it.
